children: The Indian rupee is poised to extend its advance on Monday as a deepening technology rout has strengthened expectations of sustained foreign buying in local equities.
is expected to open in the 92.60-92.64 range, per traders, having settled at 92.67 to the dollar on Friday.

The rupee advanced in every trading session last week, with the rally accelerating on Friday as heavy dollar sales by foreign banks, on behalf of custodial clients, pushed the currency well past the 93-per-dollar level.

The Indian unit has come a long way over the last six weeks. The currency, which threatened to slide past 97 per dollar, has staged a significant recovery on the back of central bank intervention and measures to rein in dollar demand.

Now, a rotation away from AI-heavy markets is providing fresh impetus. Foreign investors are expected to continue to channel money into Indian equities as the selloff in technology stocks gathered pace on Friday, with the Nasdaq Composite sliding more than 5%.
Overseas investors poured more than $1 billion into Indian equities on Friday, extending a buying spree that has already brought $12.9 billion into the market this month.
"The strength of the flows we are seeing is pushing the rupee to levels that few would have thought possible just a few weeks back," a currency trader at a private sector bank said.
"The rally looks extremely overstretched and the currency appears overbought. While these levels look unsustainable, you can't argue with the price action."
The rupee could draw further support on Monday from a slight paring back of expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike in December amid heightened risk aversion.
While a 25-basis-point increase remains the most likely outcome, it is no longer fully priced in, with markets assigning a small probability of no change in rates.
